opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Miller (employee ID E017) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E017.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jennifer Miller (E017) is a full-time Analyst. She requests write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, write is permitted (admin would require owning the system, which she does not). Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Jennifer Miller (E017) is a contractor with basic security training (not advanced). Contractors never get admin; write requires advanced training, which she does not have. Requested write exceeds her maximum of read, so recommend read for Source Code.
reason: The Security agent's database lookup indicates Jennifer Miller (E017) is a contractor with basic security training (not advanced). Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training. Since she does not have advanced training, her maximum access to Source Code is read. The requested write exceeds that maximum, so I grant the maximum of read. (Note: HR lists her as full-time, but given the conflicting employment records and the Security verification of contractor status with basic training, the safer/restrictive maximum applies.)
